hints.content:
First, let's change the second factor into scientific notation.

$(1.3\times 10^{-2}) \times (0.05) = (1.3\times 10^{-2}) \times (5.0\times 10^{-2}) $

Start by collecting the significands and exponents.

 $ (\blue{1.3} \times \pink{10^{-2}}) \times (\blue{5.0} \times \pink{10^{-2}}) = (\blue{1.3} \times \blue{5.0}) \times (\pink{10^{-2}} \times \pink{10^{-2}}) $

Then multiply each term separately. When multiplying exponents with the same base, add the powers together.

 $= \blue{6.5} \times \pink{10^{-2 \,+\, -2}}$

 $= \blue{6.5} \times \pink{10^{-4}}$
